Light sleep exits in one cycle (R01).

quantity: Wake energy per MB of domain (CORRECTED 2026-10-08; see EXP-0009A)
value: Supply energy of a hard-switched rail recharged from V_active: E = C x V_active x dV per rail (KNOWN: the supply delivers Q = C dV at V_active; half is stored, half dissipated in the switch). Components per decimal MB (8e6 cells), LOW / PLANNING / HIGH: (a) cell-rail capacitance 0.3 / 0.5 / 1.0 fF per cell = 2.4 / 4 / 8 nF per MB, swing V_ret -> V_active (0.35 -> 0.75 V, dV 0.40 V): 0.72 / 1.20 / 2.40 nJ; (b) bitline restore, two bitlines per column at 0.10 / 0.15 / 0.20 fF per cell per line = 1.6 / 2.4 / 3.2 nF per MB, swing dV (LOW, PLANNING: bitlines follow the array rail) or full V_active (HIGH: bitlines discharged in retention): 0.48 / 0.72 / 1.80 nJ; (c) periphery virtual rail, full V_active swing, 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.6 nF per MB (R11: ~2.6 nF per mm2 of logic x ~0.3 mm2 of periphery per MB at EXP-0006 densities): 0.23 / 0.45 / 0.90 nJ; (d) decoupling and grid at 10% / 20% / 50% of the switched capacitance (R11 uses 20%): 0.14 / 0.47 / 2.55 nJ. RETENTION_VRET exit = a+b+c+d = 1.57 / 2.84 / 7.65 nJ per MB; DEEP_SLEEP_NOMINAL exit = b+c+d (array rail unchanged); LIGHT_SLEEP exit = b (bitline precharge only). Sequencer 10 pJ per macro. Sleep entry: 0 supply energy (the stored rail charge is dissipated, not drawn). In-rush (all four components, planning): 3.8 nC per MB -> 0.97 nC per 256 KB macro / 200 ns = 4.9 mA per macro, 39 mA per group of 8 (consistent with B6 planning); HIGH 2.6 mA per macro at 1 us; LOW (10 ns per macro, 64 in parallel, from R03's 4 KB segments) implies 54 mA per macro and 3.4 A per group, so the LOW latency level is not in-rush-consistent for 256 KB macros and is a latency bound only. SUPERSEDED: EXP-0009 (commit 899976e) stated the same formula and 4 nF/MB but applied 1.2 uJ/MB (1000x the formula's 1.2 nJ/MB) as the RETENTION_VRET exit, with PLANNING 0.15 and LOW 0.02 uJ/MB derived from it; 1.2 uJ/MB would require 4 uF per MB and ~2 A of in-rush per macro at the B6 wake time. R03's 41-cycle break-even implies ~6 pJ/MB for its source-biased SLEEP exit, 200x below (a); R03 is used for latency and ratios only. No measured modern-node macro wake energy exists; the range spans ~5x.
label: ASSUMPTION (physics-based component estimate; R11 T2 method and capacitance density; dimensional check by test)

Independent array-voltage regulation per macro is NOT assumed: V_ret is a shared retention rail per domain.

No physical clock is claimed; EXP-0005 RTL is cycle-exact but unclocked.

quantity: Shutdown-and-reload idle policy (PX) (CORRECTED 2026-10-08; see EXP-0009A, B16, B17)
value: NOT a retention mode (data lost). Between sessions the array is powered off (residual switch leakage 0.002 x active, R03) and the weights are reloaded at the next session from a PERSISTENT backing store whose standby, reload energy, bandwidth and latency are charged explicitly: B16 (LPDDR-backed) or B17 (flash-backed). SUPERSEDED: EXP-0009 (899976e) charged only the SRAM residual while idle, priced the reload at the LPDDR path energy (13.2 mJ for Falcon-E 1B) but timed it at flash-class 1-4 GB/s, and gave the persistent copy no standby cost; that row is kept as PX-UNBACKED (superseded) for traceability only.
label: comparison policy; backing memory priced by B16/B17

value: The weights' persistent copy sits in the LPDDR5X die that the system has anyway for head/KV. Reload energy = weights x 8 x (4.0 pJ/bit LPDDR read path, B10 + 0.50 pJ/bit SRAM write path = EXP-0008 resident path with the macro write 54.1/32.8 x read, E01) = 14.3 mJ for Falcon-E 1B; reload time = weights / (17.07 GB/s x 70%) = 33 ms. Backing standby while idle = the DRAM's data-retaining idle mode at the idle temperature (self-refresh 0.77-9.8 mW for gaps >= 1 s, power-down otherwise, B10); in the WEIGHTS-ONLY view the DRAM also sits in power-down (5.4 mW) during the session because nothing else uses it, in the SYSTEM view (head/KV external) that background is already counted on both sides. Consequence: in the weights-only view PX-DRAM idle power is never below the streaming baseline's idle power (same die, same mode), so PX-DRAM can only win through the session, never through the gap.
label: T1 datasheet modes (E06) + EXP-0008 energies; boundary stated

value: The persistent copy sits in a UFS-class NAND device. Read energy LOW 46 / PLANNING 93 / HIGH 171 pJ/bit (R19: 2-lane datasheet max 92.8 pJ/bit at 2 GB/s; 1-lane 171; LOW = half the 2-lane maximum as a typical-vs-max allowance, same convention as EXP-0008 A6; R21's independent 102.4 pJ/bit incl. I/O corroborates) plus 0.50 pJ/bit SRAM write path; reload bandwidth 4 / 2 / 1 GB/s (R19 2-lane 2,000 MB/s and 1-lane 1,000 MB/s; 4 GB/s = UFS 4.0 class, EXP-0008 A10 upper bound); first-token latency 0.10 / 0.20 / 0.40 s for Falcon-E 1B; standby while idle 0 / 0.43 / 0.58 mW (R19 PowerDown with host re-init (resume cost not modeled) / Sleep / Hibernate; R20 0.2 mW corroborates). Host-side UFS controller and M-PHY energy is not in any datasheet read and is covered only by the HIGH level. Flash is also what the streaming baseline would reload its DRAM from if it powered the DRAM off for long gaps; that symmetric variant is priced as a baseline row (DRAM off, flash reload at the same pJ/bit + 4.0 pJ/bit DRAM write).
label: T1 datasheet (R19) device-side; host side ASSUMPTION; T3 corroboration (R20, R21)

value: B4's RETENTION_VRET ratio uses array POWER at V_ret, I(V_ret) x V_ret, which is the supply draw only if the retention rail is delivered at V_ret by an efficient converter or a separate supply pin (R01 is dual-rail). If V_ret is derived on-die from V_dd by a linear element (source-bias diode as in R04's light/deep sleep, or an LDO), the supply still delivers at V_dd and the ratio becomes the CURRENT ratio I(V_ret)/I(V_nom) = power ratio x V_nom/V_ret = 2.0x worse at 0.35 V (0.076 -> 0.152 at 25 C; 0.231 -> 0.462 at 85 C). Planning keeps the separate-rail case; the linear case is a sensitivity row and an open founder question.
label: ASSUMPTION; verdict-relevant at 85 C

quantity: Resident-side DRAM background in the system view (sensitivity)
value: In the head/KV-inclusive comparison the streaming side carries its LPDDR background (busy fraction x IDD2N + rest x IDD2P) while the resident side's head/KV traffic was charged energy only. A sensitivity column charges the resident side the same background function evaluated on its head+KV bytes. Residual asymmetry: the streaming side's background is evaluated on its weight bytes only (its head/KV traffic rides the same channel and is charged energy only), so the column is conservative against residency, not exact.
label: boundary disclosure

value: JEDEC/Micron IDD values are specified at the maximum operating case temperature, so the IDD2N (32.1 mW) and IDD2P (5.4 mW) charged during generation are hot-corner maxima at every temperature while the SRAM side uses 25 C measurements at 25 C. This favours residency at 25 C by up to ~27 mW of the 345 mW LPDDR total (Falcon-E 1B at 25 tok/s). Planning is left as EXP-0008 defined it; a sensitivity row halves IDD2N/IDD2P at 25 C.
label: disclosure

value: sessions of N tokens at R tok/s separated by idle gaps G; duty cycle d = active time fraction at 25 tok/s; these are usage sweeps, not forecasts.
label: sweep definition
